what: Becton Dickinson makes medical supplies: syringes and needles, infusion pumps, catheters, diagnostic instruments and laboratory equipment. It is preparing to separate its biosciences and diagnostics business.
customers: Hospitals, clinics, laboratories, pharmaceutical companies and health systems worldwide.
money: syringes, infusion systems, pharmaceutical delivery devices
moat: Products used by the billion across hospital systems with purchasing contracts and regulatory approvals that make substitution slow.
risks: Growth has been slow at about 5% a year over three years
Debt of about $17 billion from past acquisitions
Return on invested capital is low at around 5%
Regulatory warnings on infusion pumps have cost time and money
opportunities: Separating the biosciences and diagnostics business should let both be valued on their own
Pharmaceutical injectable delivery grows with GLP-1 and biologic medicines
Cost programmes are lifting margins from a low base
watch: Organic revenue growth and the timetable for the Life Sciences separation.
